findings.title: Demo action protocol is documented as returning 204
findings.evidence: The action protocol dispatches schema-bearing requests to actionTurn and returns a typed JSON rules proposal in demo mode. The legacy response branch returns 204.
findings.impact: An integrator can discard or mishandle the current protocol response by implementing the documented demo 204 expectation.
findings.fix: Describe demo action-protocol 200 JSON and legacy-shape 204 separately; documentation correction only.

findings.title: Route map claims universal Origin and capability enforcement
findings.evidence: Research has no route-level Origin, capability or rate guard. Art and agent use foreignOrigin, which allows absent Origin. The shared API wrapper does not install these guards. Token/signature routes also use their own trust rules.
findings.impact: Security-sensitive documentation can lead consumers and reviewers to rely on controls that selected handlers do not enforce. P0 describes misinformation under the user's taxonomy, not an exploitability or runtime vulnerability rating.
findings.fix: Replace the universal sentence with route-specific guard/trust semantics and link the exact HTTP catalog.

findings.title: Current analytics deployment claim contradicts hosted rollout receipts
findings.evidence: The touched runtime page says no deployment sets GA variables and every deployment collects nothing today. The same candidate records the 2026-10-11 hosted configuration, collection and a subsequent 63406e1 follow-up.
findings.impact: An operator can mistake dated default-off setup guidance for current host state. This is an incorrect deployment claim (P1); no fresh live readback or new collection behavior was established.
findings.fix: Preserve default-off semantics while replacing the blanket host assertion with dated, scoped rollout evidence and a fresh-verification requirement.

findings.title: Placeholder tenant is explained as absence of any app tenant concept
findings.evidence: The app derives anonymous, account and device tenant context. The Ticketmaster mapper intentionally uses placeholder scope, and the public research route does not inject trusted scope.
findings.impact: The integration explanation misdirects identity work toward an already existing app concept rather than the actual mapper/route trust-wiring gap.
findings.fix: Attribute the placeholder to unwired trusted tenant/project context in this integration boundary.

findings.title: POST events borrows capability and admin controls from GET
findings.evidence: POST checks Origin, rate, 2 KiB JSON size and client-event type; if project is supplied it rejects role none. It does not invoke requireCapability or require admin.view for an unscoped event. GET has the stated admin/capability checks.
findings.impact: The documented POST trust boundary is materially stronger than the implementation. P0 rates security-sensitive misinformation only, not the unchanged endpoint's exploitability.
findings.fix: Document POST's exact guards, optional project role rejection and unscoped anonymous possibility, separately from GET.

findings.title: Email-change confirmation is said to create a session cookie
findings.evidence: The email-change branch consumes the link and changes email before a 303 redirect without a session cookie. The sign-in branch starts a session and supplies its cookie.
findings.impact: A client integrating account email confirmation can falsely rely on an authenticated session being established.
findings.fix: State distinct successful sign-in and email-change outcomes.

findings.title: Auth-confirm form parsing is described as a universal 4 KiB byte ceiling
findings.evidence: JSON uses readJson(req,4096). Form parsing checks declared Content-Length, then reads the whole body and applies JavaScript text.length > 4096. That is a post-read code-unit check, not an equivalent streaming byte cap for missing/inaccurate Content-Length.
findings.impact: Integrators receive an inaccurate request-boundary contract. P1 concerns protocol/integration documentation; no live capacity or exploit claim was made.
findings.fix: Describe the JSON streaming byte cap and the form declared-length/post-read code-unit checks separately.

findings.title: Lexical guard descriptions are narrower than the implemented predicates
findings.evidence: isCredential checks string length 1–8192, trim equality, and absence of code units below33 or equal127. Embedded non-ASCII whitespace/C1 controls can reach the verifier. CAPABILITY is /^[a-z][\w.:-]{0,127}$/u, permitting uppercase letters after the first character, underscore, dot, colon or hyphen; a dot is not required.
findings.reproduction: Read the exact own source predicates and their call sites at merged51fd or observedcurrentmain7d861; source blobs match. Examples a\u00a0b and a\u0085b satisfy the local credential predicate, and finance.READ or finance:read satisfy CAPABILITY. These are static predicate consequences, not endpoint/authentication tests.
findings.impact: A host integrator can rely on an inaccurate local syntax precheck. The docs already place authenticity, signature and session authority in the injected verifier, and required grants are checked by exact finance.read/finance.export strings, so no authorization bypass or exploit claim is made. P2 rates incomplete precision in the explanation.

fix.credential: The credential must be a nonempty string of at most8192 UTF-16 code units, unchanged by String.trim(). The package rejects U+0000–U+0020 and U+007F anywhere before invoking the verifier; it does not reject every Unicode whitespace/control character. The host verifier remains responsible for credential format, signature, live session and membership validation.
fix.capability: Capability entries must match /^[a-z][\w.:-]{0,127}$/u: a lowercase ASCII initial followed by up to127 ASCII word characters, dots, colons or hyphens. A dot is not mandatory and later letters may be uppercase. Authorization requires exact finance.read/finance.export strings from the permission matrix.
